speed-regression.purpose: Rust speed and memory have not regressed
speed-regression.reference: reference/perf_baseline.json, accepted on the same machine and toolchain
speed-regression.criterion: no workload's median outside the baseline's range and over 10% slower
speed-regression.note: no workload slower than the baseline

rust-tests.purpose: Rust unit, integration, and mission regression tests; formatting; lints; tests of these checking tools
rust-tests.criterion: every test passes, no lint or format finding

rust-determinism.purpose: worker counts, recording, tracing on shipped missions, and spatial lookup method change no output
rust-determinism.criterion: byte-identical frames, events, and summaries on every mission and workload

cpp-agreement.purpose: behaviour matches C++ SCRIMMAGE on the curated missions (reference/missions.txt)
cpp-agreement.reference: C++ SCRIMMAGE in Docker: the unmodified and comparison branches
cpp-agreement.criterion: states within tolerance, identical deliveries, summaries equal or explained, C++ instrumentation and Rust variants byte-identical

cpp-long.purpose: agreement over ten 1,000 s scenarios (seed 7), and whether late divergence is the port or the dynamics
cpp-long.reference: C++ SCRIMMAGE; Rust after one-ulp nudges
cpp-long.criterion: every run finishes cleanly with explained summaries; divergence is reported

cpp-noise.purpose: sensor noise matches sample for sample, and by distribution
cpp-noise.criterion: the case passes (samples within tolerance); no KS test below the Bonferroni threshold

checker-sensitivity.purpose: the C++ comparison catches plausible porting bugs
checker-sensitivity.criterion: an unmodified control passes; every planted bug is caught

speed-cpp-container.purpose: C++ and Rust speed and memory in one Linux container
speed-cpp-container.reference: C++ SCRIMMAGE comparison branch, same container
speed-cpp-container.criterion: Rust identical at 1 and 8 workers and to C++ where both draw the same numbers

speed-cpp-native.purpose: C++ and Rust speed and memory on bare-metal macOS

speed-spatial.purpose: collision checking cost with the scan and with grids
speed-spatial.reference: the scan, which tests every contact

speed-messages.purpose: message routing cost with all-agent traffic

rk4-loads.purpose: what evaluating forces at every RK4 stage changes
rk4-loads.reference: unmodified C++ SCRIMMAGE, which holds forces through the step

multirotor-control.purpose: MultirotorVelocityController's step responses on the Crazyflie, and convergence as the step shrinks
multirotor-control.reference: the commands; Förster's rotor drag; the 20-substep run
multirotor-control.criterion: every velocity error within 5% over the last second, Crazyflie drag tilt within 2%, 5 substeps within 5 mm

rascal-control.purpose: AircraftPIDController's rascal settings on FixedWing6DOF's Rascal: altitude derivative gain after upsets, and steps under each attitude limit
rascal-control.criterion: altitude D changes the error under 1 cm; under the rascal limits every step settles and pitch stays under 25 degrees

simple-aircraft-fit.purpose: SimpleAircraft's rascal limits against FixedWing6DOF's Rascal: speeds, acceleration, climb, descent, turn rate, and attitude rates
simple-aircraft-fit.criterion: every SimpleAircraft number within 5% (or 0.2) of the Rascal's

rotors-motor.purpose: Multirotor's motor lag and rotor loads against RotorS, sample by sample, and the Crazyflie's and Firefly's whole-vehicle loads against the sum of RotorS's rotor loads at held states
rotors-motor.reference: RotorS's motor-plugin source (ethz-asl/rotors_simulator), compiled in Docker
rotors-motor.criterion: every sample within 1e-12 relative; samples equal the committed fixture

crazyflow-crazyflie.purpose: Multirotor's Crazyflie and Firefly loads at held states against Crazyflow's first-principles dynamics, and the Crazyflie flown against it in five open-loop flights (four airborne near hover, one spin-up stress case) with the same constants and motor commands
crazyflow-crazyflie.criterion: every held state within 1e-12 of the rotor loads and equal to the committed fixture; every flight without rotor drag, and with Ripple's hub drag fed into Crazyflow, within limits set from the step-size sensitivities (1e-9 m, 1e-9 m/s, 1e-10 rad, 1e-10 rad/s), which each run measures again; the lumped-drag difference is reported

jsbsim-rascal.purpose: FixedWing6DOF's Rascal against ArduPilot's JSBSim Rascal: loads at a grid of held states, sample by sample, and 5 s open-loop glides
jsbsim-rascal.reference: JSBSim (the jsbsim package, pinned, run with uv) on ArduPilot's Rascal files at a pinned commit
jsbsim-rascal.criterion: every grid sample within the Rust test's limit and equal to the committed fixture; every glide within 0.2 m in JSBSim's elevator-drag form

stall-landing.purpose: whether stall tables change ArduPlane's Rascal landing
stall-landing.reference: the same mission without tables, and a repeat of it

source_note: After the run, comments in crates/cli/src/sweep.rs and crates/core/src/parse/yaml_mission.rs changed (source 29ead33e5bef to c534d4f90c4f); the rebuilt release executable was byte-identical.
